A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Prior Learning in Introspective VAEs. Their main text, equations, experimental results and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial formatting changes and relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original density-estimation and image-generation experiments, representation evaluations, regularization ablations and encoder-behavior studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds precision/recall results and further illustrative evidence concerning inactive prior modes.

M1.justification: v2 specifies H(C) as the responsibility regularizer; v3 Section 4.2.3 specifies normalized entropy H_n(C)=H(C)/log(M). This revises the stated loss scaling, although an implementation change is not established. The prior–decoder cooperation, clipping and stop-gradient procedures remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 8Gaussian, 2Spirals, Checkerboard, Rings, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. The synthetic distribution-overlap scenarios used to study encoder behavior also already appear in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: The ordinary VAE baseline, standard-Gaussian S-IntroVAE, fixed/trainable MoG configurations and baseline-reproduction comparisons retain their membership. Revised VampPrior/MoG labels clarify the existing warm-up and adversarial-training stages.

E3.justification: v3 adds generative precision and recall to the image-evaluation metrics in Section 5.2. Existing density metrics, FID, classification evaluations, prior component counts, 20-epoch image warm-up and Monte Carlo KL procedure are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a precision/recall diagnostic for possible memorization and generated-sample examples identifying inactive-mode outputs in Figure 3b. The component-count and entropy-regularization sweeps, clipping ablation and encoder-overfitting study were already present in v2.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes from mean ± standard deviation to mean ± standard error over the same five seeds. Tables 2 and 5 newly specify standard errors and three image-experiment runs, which v2 did not explicitly identify. No increase in runs is established; Table 4 retains standard deviations.

E6.justification: v3 retains the existing benchmark mean scores while adding precision/recall entries in Tables 2 and 5; for example, MNIST with the standard Gaussian has recall 0.565 and precision 0.522. Figure 3b adds per-mode generation examples. Smaller uncertainty values accompany the reporting change identified under E5.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.4 derives linear versus quadratic scaling of mean and standard-deviation gradients with standardized sample displacement, motivating variance clipping. Appendix C.3 also corrects the distinction between exact KL divergence and its Monte Carlo estimate. The existing equilibrium results, assumptions and proofs remain substantively intact.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first integration of prior learning into Introspective VAEs through prior–decoder cooperation, preservation of the equilibrium characterization, two regularizers and benefits for generation and representation learning. Changing 'benefit' to 'effect' does not materially alter the retained conclusions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses the standard-Gaussian advantage on 8Gaussian and proposes a stability–multimodality tradeoff explanation. It also interprets the new precision/recall results as showing no memorization pattern and develops the explanation of variance explosions. These extend the earlier interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: New Algorithm 1 documents update sequencing, Adam updates, input-dimension loss scaling, MoG sampling and regularization operations. Footnote 2 explains how the warm-up VampPrior parameters initialize the MoG. These improve implementation documentation without establishing that the underlying implementation was replaced.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on latent-space structure and scientific discovery, including Shrivastava, Oring, Leeb and Wang, plus Kynkäänniemi et al. for precision/recall evaluation. Its positioning relative to S-IntroVAE, CS-IntroVAE, VampPrior and DeLiGAN remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 groups theory and implementation under Section 4, promotes the existing encoder study into Section 4.1.2, clarifies prior configurations and rewrites portions of the introduction and experimental discussion. Most exposition and the overall narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to predominantly one column. Figure 1 is rearranged, the encoder-study figure is enlarged and reorganized, Figure 3 combines regularization illustrations, and existing latent plots are combined in main-text Figure 5. Algorithm 1, redesigned table headers and precision/recall rows substantially revise the presentation.

improvement.justification: Algorithm 1 and explicit uncertainty/run descriptions make the work easier to reproduce and assess. The variance derivation, precision/recall diagnostic and discussion of the 8Gaussian exception strengthen supporting explanations. These gains are limited: the central claims and retained mean results remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether the revised entropy scaling reflects an implementation change.
